paragraphs: R. Chananyah, son of R. Abbahu. R. Elazar son of R. Yosi, in the name of R. Chananyah son of R. Abbahu: an incident, etc. Again R. Elazar son of R. Yosi said: an incident, etc.; Rabbi heard and said, etc.; R. Shimon ben Chalafta heard, etc.: Eikhah Rabbah, on “He ground my teeth with gravel.” Apparently this R. Elazar son of R. Yosi is [the son of] R. Yosi ben Chalafta. If so, this R. Chananyah son of R. Abbahu is early, and is not the R. Chanina son of R. Abbahu above, for he is early. However, that matter in Kohelet Rabbah, on “All things are wearying,” says: R. Elazar, in the name of R. Chanina son of R. Abbahu, an incident, etc.; again, R. Elazar in R. Yosi's name, etc.; Rabbi heard, etc. On this basis one may say that this R. Elazar is the unqualified R. Elazar ben Pedat. But this too is not so, since R. Abbahu frequently spoke in R. Elazar's name. How could R. Elazar speak in the name of R. Chanina, R. Abbahu's son?
